rv.q: A promising start for Byrne then – and a triumphant one for Ali.
Sharp lines and strong characterisation overwhelm a slightly stagnant story, but Ali keeps the audience laughing.
This piece has plenty of energy and potential but it needs more structure and development in its storytelling – as it stands, it feels as if it’s just beginning as it comes to the end.
A truly remarkable and refreshing piece of theatre – when it comes to things I can fault about it, there really is nothing.
It is a perfect example of how the arts can and should be used to create social and political change.
Ali herself has no such problem, as she keeps the laughs coming in a way that effortlessly show us the characters and community she wants us to share in.

cn.t: Critics praise this sassy British-Somali riff on The Breakfast Club for its sharp dialogue and strong characterization, though some find the story slightly stagnant. The teen comedy delights with its fresh perspective and humor.
